properties.name: LESSON: after the base of a stacked PR squash-merges, merging main into the stack conflicts on every file the base touched — and resolving toward main reverts the stacked work with no error; only the coherence gate noticed
properties.statement:
WHAT HAPPENED, 2026-09-14, PR #504 stacked on #503. #503 squash-merged. `git merge origin/main` into the stacked branch conflicted on ALL EIGHT files #503 had touched — a squash rewrites their history, so git sees both sides changed. The resolution loop took `origin/main`'s side for every conflict. Six of those files were the ones carrying #504's NEW detector; main's side did not have it. The merge committed cleanly. The detector was gone from the branch and nothing in git said so.

WHAT CAUGHT IT: `reflow2_check` — the two-sided checksums accepted into the graph for #504's files no longer matched the files on disk, so the gate FAILED on drift before anything was pushed. A git-only workflow would have pushed a PR whose description promised a detector its diff did not contain.

THE RULE: after the base squash-merges, do NOT bulk-resolve a merge toward main. Either `git rebase --onto origin/main <old-base-tip>` so only the stacked commits replay, or resolve each conflicted file by taking the STACKED branch's version and diffing it against main by hand. If a merge has already been committed, restore the stacked files from the pre-merge tip (`git checkout HEAD^1 -- <files>`) as a visible commit — never rewrite.

WHY THIS IS A DESIGN LESSON AND NOT ONLY A GIT ONE: the accepted checksum is the design's own record of "this is the file that realizes this capability", and it is the ONLY thing in the whole toolchain that compared the branch to its own promise. That is `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`'s neighbour — a record that lets a later check say "what you shipped is not what you said".



SECOND INSTANCE, HANDLED THE OTHER WAY, 2026-10-07: #695 was stacked on #694, and #694 squash-merged. Merging main into #695 conflicted on the hub skill, its two mirrors and tools/skill_lint.py. The stacked side was a superset of main's for every one of them (main's version was #694's own content), so each conflict was resolved toward the STACK, not toward main. Verified with git diff origin/main showing exactly slice 2's change, then reflow2_check OK, and CI green after one unrelated clippy fix. The rule this lesson implies: after a squash of the base, the stacked side usually wins, so check with a diff against main rather than resolving by habit.
